findings.title: Error timestamps (seconds) compared against replay event timestamps (milliseconds)
findings.body: `fetch_error_details` copies the nodestore event `timestamp`, which is float epoch seconds, into `ErrorEvent`. `gen_request_data` compares it with `event.get("timestamp", 0)` from the rrweb recording segments, which are epoch milliseconds. Every error therefore compares as earlier than the first replay event. All errors are emitted at the top of the log instead of interleaved chronologically, and the 'at <ts>' text mixes units. The tests hide this because they use the same small or second-scale values on both sides. Convert one side (for example multiply the error timestamp by 1000) so the units match.

findings.title: zip(error_ids, events.values()) can pair event IDs with the wrong nodestore payloads
findings.body: `nodestore.backend.get_multi(node_ids)` returns a dict keyed by node ID. It is not guaranteed to preserve input order, and missing nodes may be omitted. Zipping `error_ids` with `events.values()` therefore misaligns IDs and data whenever any node is missing or the order differs. The `id` field of the resulting `ErrorEvent` can then be attached to the wrong error. Look each event up with `events.get(node_id)` while iterating `zip(error_ids, node_ids)`.

findings.title: Snuba replay query runs even when error context is disabled
findings.body: `query_replay_instance` and `process_raw_response` always run, and `enable_error_context=false` is only checked afterwards. When the caller opts out of error context, the extra Snuba round trip is wasted and adds latency to every summarize request. Check the flag first and skip the query entirely when it is false.

findings.title: age/timestamp exclusivity validation is incomplete and truthiness-based
findings.body: `validate_timestamp` and `validate_age` only run when their own field is present. A report with neither `age` nor `timestamp` therefore passes validation, although the spec requires one of them. The cross-check uses `self.initial_data.get("age")` / `.get("timestamp")` truthiness, so a value of `0` (valid for `timestamp`, allowed for `age`) is treated as absent. A report containing both `age: 0` and `timestamp` is accepted. Use `"age" in self.initial_data` and add an object-level `validate()` requiring exactly one of the two fields.

findings.title: Feature-flagged TableWidgetVisualization renders hardcoded empty data
findings.body: When `use-table-widget-visualization` is enabled, the widget renders `TableWidgetVisualization` with `columns={[]}` and a hardcoded empty `tableData`. It ignores `result.data`, `result.meta`, `fieldAliases`, the custom field renderers, the `loading` handling and the title. Every table widget for an org with the flag on would show an empty table. Either wire the real result data and metadata through or do not ship this branch.

findings.title: Analytics event recorded before the feature-flag check
findings.body: `analytics.record("preprod_artifact.api.assemble", ...)` fires before the `organizations:preprod-artifact-assemble` check. Requests from orgs without the feature, which are answered with 404, are still counted as assemble API usage. This inflates the metric and records events for a disabled feature. Move the call after the feature gate.

findings.title: Query key omits organization slug
findings.body: The react-query key is `['use-trace-item-attribute-keys', queryOptions]`, and `queryOptions` contains only itemType, attributeType, project IDs, search and date params. The organization is not part of the key. Switching organizations with the same page filters and project IDs can serve cached attribute keys from the previous org. Include `organization.slug` in the key, as the previous `useApiQuery` path-based key did.
